findings.trigger: An installation that still has web_config.json with a non-empty 'advanced_settings' (e.g. from an earlier v1.1.x-> virtual-modular migration, or any pre-real-modular install) starts up and ensure_modular_structure() decides a real modular migration is needed (needs_real_modular_migration, :96). perform_real_modular_migration (:140) calls migrate_web_configs_to_files (:347), which copies only web_ui_user/web_ui_password_hash/admin_enabled/session_timeout/donation_disable_key/scheduler_debug_mode into web_ui.json and explicitly does NOT copy 'advanced_settings' - its own log line at :364 says the settings are 'kept in web_config.json'. Immediately afterwards, in the same perform_real_modular_migration run, cleanup_legacy_files_after_migration (:195) deletes web_config.json because it is in legacy_files_to_remove (:202). From then on ConfigLoaderService._legacy_advanced_settings()/load_real_modular_config (services/config/config_loader_service.py:145-149, :206-213) can no longer find web_config.json, so 'advanced_settings' resolves to {} on every future load: whatever the operator had configured there (advanced/env overrides) silently reads back empty, with no error and no warning message anywhere in this code path.
findings.suggestion: Either carry 'advanced_settings' from web_config.json into the new modular structure inside migrate_web_configs_to_files (e.g. write it into config.json's advanced_settings, the way migrate_system_configs_to_files builds config.json), or stop deleting web_config.json in cleanup_legacy_files_after_migration until there is an on-disk home for those settings in the modular layout.

findings.trigger: process_config_form always executes `updated_config['heartbeat'] = ConfigFormParserService._parse_heartbeat(form_data)` (:521), and _parse_heartbeat (:367-386) returns {'enabled': False, 'ping_url': '', 'interval': 5} whenever 'heartbeat_ping_url' is missing from form_data or is not an https:// URL. Unlike channel_permissions, which is only overwritten when the form actually 'contained the channel tables' (checked via the explicit 'channel_tables_submitted' marker at :516, precisely because this codebase already has a precedent of forms that post only part of the settings page), there is no equivalent guard for the heartbeat block: any call to process_config_form whose form_data happens not to carry 'heartbeat_ping_url' resets a previously configured, working Status Watchdog URL to disabled/empty, with nothing in the response message pointing this out.
findings.suggestion: Give the heartbeat block the same submitted-marker guard already used for channel_permissions (channel_tables_submitted), so that a request without heartbeat_ping_url leaves the stored heartbeat configuration untouched instead of resetting it.
findings.unsure_why: This section does not include the web templates/JS that build the request(s) calling process_config_form, so it cannot be confirmed whether the one settings page that saves configuration always includes heartbeat_ping_url (in which case this path is unreachable in practice) or whether, like the channel tables, it can also be posted/omitted separately.

notes: Two smaller observations that did not get their own finding slot because they sit in the same function as F2 (process_config_form) and the report format allows only one 'finding' reference per PLAN name: (1) In process_config_form, if channels_saved is False the function returns `(updated_config, False, CHANNELS_NOT_SAVED_MESSAGE)` at :620, discarding the whole 'message' string built above it - including the password-changed notice ('...log in again with the new password', :584-585), the refused-heartbeat-URL warning, the unusable/duplicate channel-ID warnings, and the donation-key warning. So if a web UI password change and a channel-file save failure happen in the same request, the operator is told only that channel permissions were not saved and is not reminded that their password already changed. Concrete but low/medium impact (file services/config/config_form_parser_service.py, lines 581-620). (2) config_form_parser_service.py's 'process remaining form fields' loop (:560-578) writes the raw posted 'bot_token' value straight into updated_config['bot_token'] with no encryption performed in this file; this section has no visibility into config_service.save_config, so it cannot be confirmed here whether encryption/token handling downstream is correct - flagging only because SPEC Z9 depends on it and the call site is outside this section's source.
